content: Possible Side Effects In the United States, if you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions Before starting maraviroc, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Maraviroc may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Maraviroc may be part of a treatment plan to reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, it is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products that may interact with maraviroc include orlistat and St. John’s Wort. Overdose If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests Before starting maraviroc and during treatment, your doctor may order laboratory tests such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, and T-cell counts. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning Maraviroc may rarely cause serious liver problems. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may occur before liver problems develop. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, rash, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, or extreme fatigue. Refer to the Side Effects section for additional details. Uses Maraviroc is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This decreases the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. Maraviroc belongs to a class of drugs known as entry inhibitors. It is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items (such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors) that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. How to Use Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting maraviroc and each time you get a refill. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, also read the Instructions for Use. The manufacturer advises against splitting, crushing, or chewing the tablet before taking it. However, some similar drugs (immediate-release tablets) may be split, crushed, or chewed. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure the dose using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. To achieve the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. Side Effects Common side effects may include cough, stomach pain, or fatigue. Lightheadedness or dizziness, especially when standing, may also occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects.
